props.gloss_en: a meduvlelet sukkah is valid
and one whose shade exceeds its sun is valid
one thick like a house, even though the stars are not seen from inside it, is valid
what is meduvlelet? Rav: a poor sukkah
and Shmuel: one reed rising and one reed descending
Rav teaches one [law]: a meduvlelet sukkah -- that is, a sparse one -- whose shade exceeds its sun is valid
Shmuel teaches two: meduvlelet is a jumbled sukkah, and the clause teaches two [laws] -- a jumbled sukkah is valid, and one whose shade exceeds its sun is valid
Abaye: they taught [that it is valid] only where there are not three tefachim between this and that
but if there are three tefachim between this and that -- invalid
Rava: even where there are three tefachim between this and that, we said [it is invalid] only where its roof has no tefach
but if its roof has a tefach -- valid
for we say: knock [it] down and lay [it] (chavot remi)
when it has a tefach, we say chavot remi
and when it has none, we do not say chavot remi

the Ohalot mishnah: boards of house and upper story with no plaster, aligned -- impurity under one of them renders impure [only] beneath it ...; if the upper ones lay between the lower ones -- impurity beneath them renders impure beneath all of them; above them -- opposite them up to the sky

the teaching on it: when is this said? when they have a tefach and between them an opening of a tefach; but if there is no tefach-opening between them, impurity under one of them renders impure beneath it, and between them and above them is pure
a beam projecting from one wall and not touching the other (and likewise two beams from opposite walls not touching): less than three [tefachim] -- he need not bring another beam; three -- he must
RSbG: less than four -- he need not bring another beam; four -- he must
and likewise two matched beams, neither of which can hold a brick: if together they hold a brick across its width, a tefach -- he need not bring another beam; if not -- he must
RSbG: if they hold a brick along its length, three tefachim -- he need not bring another beam; if not -- he must

if one was above and one below -- R' Yosei b'R' Yehuda: one views the upper as though below and the lower as though above, provided the upper is not above twenty amot and the lower not below ten [tefachim]
Rav Kahana: read it thus -- provided the upper is not above twenty but within twenty, and the lower adjoins it by less than three
alternatively: provided the lower is not below ten but above ten, and the upper adjoins it by less than three

supports.gloss_en: מנא אמינא לה ... דתנן: the Ohalot mishnah -- staggered upper boards make impurity spread beneath all of them (kind tanya_kevatei: corpus convention for מנא אמינא לה דתנן)
ותני עלה: במה דברים אמורים בזמן שיש בהן טפח -- אלמא כי אית ביה טפח אמרינן חבוט רמי
ותני עלה: ... אבל אין ביניהן פותח טפח ... ביניהן ועל גביהן טהור -- וכי לית ביה טפח לא אמרינן חבוט רמי

objections.gloss_en: וכל היכא דלית ביה טפח לא אמרינן חבוט רמי? והא תניא ... רואין העליונה כאילו היא למטה ... הא זה וזה בתוך עשרים — אמרינן חבוט רמי אף על גב דלית ביה טפח! (the beams of the baraita cannot each hold a brick; his inference at 22b.4)

answered_by.gloss_en: תריץ ואימא הכי: the upper within twenty and the lower adjoining it by less than three (= p_kahana_tachtona_semucha)
אי נמי: the lower above ten and the upper adjoining it by less than three; but at three, since it has no tefach, we do not say chavot remi (= p_kahana_elyona_semucha)
